key_insight: The paper gives the first finite-time convergence guarantees for exact natural policy gradient in finite-horizon MDPs, showing sublinear decay with constant steps and geometric convergence with increasing steps.
engineering_relevance: These results provide practical step-size guidance for deploying policy-gradient methods like TRPO/PPO-style optimizers in finite-horizon control problems with known dynamics.
method: Analyze exact NPG in finite-horizon MDPs with horizon-dependent transition kernels.
Prove O(H^2/t) sublinear convergence for constant step sizes in tabular and linear-MDP settings.
Establish linear geometric convergence under increasing step sizes, including a robust horizon-based schedule.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical finite-time convergence rates only, with no empirical benchmark or dataset evaluation described.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees rely on exact dynamics/known kernels and, for the linear MDP extension, an exact population-projection oracle with full-support projection distribution.
paper_title: Finite-Time Analysis of the Natural Policy Gradient in Finite-Horizon Markov Decision Processes
